title: Machine-learning image search helps identify Pavo, an isolated star-forming dwarf galaxy
summary: A search combining low-surface-brightness galaxy detection and machine-learning candidate classification identified Pavo in Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey imaging. Follow-up Magellan imaging resolved young and old stellar populations and measured a tip-of-the-red-giant-branch distance of about 1.99 Mpc, establishing Pavo as an extremely isolated, low-mass star-forming dwarf galaxy just beyond the Local Group.
ai_technology: Machine-learning image candidate classifier used with low-surface-brightness galaxy search algorithms
organization: University of Arizona; University of Chicago; University of Minnesota Duluth; and collaborators

evidence.tested: A search combining low-surface-brightness galaxy detection and machine-learning candidate classification identified Pavo in Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey imaging.
evidence.unknown: The AI contributed candidate classification within a broader image-search workflow. The discovery was verified by follow-up observations and astrophysical analysis. AAS conference abstract from 2024 also describes this same Pavo discovery and is not a separate result.
evidence.ai_role: Classified image-search candidates in DECaLS imaging; the search team selected Pavo for follow-up, and telescope imaging and color-magnitude analysis established its distance and galaxy properties.
